verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB documents full logging of every query an agent runs, replayable down to the columns it read, which gives a first-party audit trail of what was run and read. That audit claim is scoped to agent queries, and column-read tracing is not lineage of where data came from through transformations. The stock ClickHouse observability surface and the stats table are about monitoring, not explicitly auditing. Missing for 10: audit logs of who ran what across all users and clients (not just agents), user identity attribution in the logs, true column-level data lineage across tables and pipelines, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I get audit logs of who ran what and column-level lineage of where data came from

citations.quote: Every query an agent runs is logged in full, so you can replay exactly what it read, down to the column
The full ClickHouse observability surface, unchanged from stock ClickHouse, plus how to query it across the whole cluster at once
